item.title: Why Traditional Unix Permissions Fall Short — and How ACLs Fix Them
item.description:
Introduction

Well-designed APIs are the foundation of modern software architecture. They enable systems to communicate effectively, support scalability, and provide a great developer experience.

Core Principles

1. RESTful Design

  • Use standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
  • Follow resource-based URLs
  • Leverage HTTP status codes appropriately
  • Support proper content negotiation

2. Consistency

  • Maintain consistent naming conventions
  • Use predictable URL structures
  • Standardize error response formats
  • Follow the same patterns across endpoints

3. Versioning

  • Implement API versioning from the start
  • Use URL-based or header-based versioning
  • Maintain backward compatibility when possible
  • Document breaking changes clearly

Best Practices

Request/Response Design

  • Use clear, descriptive resource names
  • Implement pagination for list endpoints
  • Include relevant metadata in responses
  • Support filtering, sorting, and field selection

Error Handling

  • Return meaningful error messages
  • Use appropriate HTTP status codes
  • Provide error codes for programmatic handling
  • Include request IDs for debugging

Security

  • Implement authentication and authorization
  • Use HTTPS for all communications
  • Validate and sanitize all inputs
  • Rate limit to prevent abuse

Performance Considerations

  • Implement caching where appropriate
  • Use compression for large payloads
  • Support partial responses (field selection)
  • Optimize database queries
  • Consider async operations for long-running tasks

Documentation

  • Provide comprehensive API documentation
  • Include request/response examples
  • Document error scenarios
  • Maintain changelog for version updates

Conclusion

Good API design requires careful consideration of developer experience, performance, and maintainability. Following these practices will help create APIs that are both powerful and easy to use.
